findings.title: School bomb threats live: 'Stay vigilant' warning after 'death is near' message and evacuations
findings.summary_md: The Mirror reported that the email sent to Scottish schools was titled "DEATH IS NEAR" and read "This is Mikhail Andropov, leader of the 'Red Owl' project. We've come to destroy you. We're going to carry out a genocide against your people." Scottish papers led their front pages with the school bomb threats, and a parent described being called by her school after news sites were already reporting the threat. The message matched threats sent to schools across the UK and Europe.

findings.title: Bomb threat at 6,000 schools; Meloni: 'They want to create fear and chaos'. She calls a meeting with the opposition
findings.summary_md: Il Sole 24 Ore reported that around 6,000 schools across Italy received emails containing bomb threats, though not all were evacuated. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called a meeting at Palazzo Chigi to coordinate the response, and Interior Minister Matteo Piantedosi said it was too early to speak of joint leadership. Defense Minister Guido Crosetto framed the threats as a strategy of terror, and similar threats were reported in Scotland and the UK.

findings.title: Thousands of schools evacuated in UK and across Europe after bomb threats
findings.summary_md: Metro reported that the "Red Owl" signature and Mikhail Andropov name had also appeared on threatening emails sent to European television stations the previous week, and that a similar email reached 271 Italian schools on November 2 claiming to be from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Hoax bomb threats had already hit schools across Scotland and Northern Ireland in October, with as many as 300 schools receiving messages before 9am. The reporting establishes the November 11 wave as the latest in a multi-wave campaign rather than an isolated incident.

findings.title: Taiwan university email linked to bomb threats against 6,000 Italian schools
findings.summary_md: Focus Taiwan reported that a Taiwan university's alumni email account was allegedly hacked and used to send bomb threat emails to more than 6,000 public schools across Italy on November 11, citing Italian media reports. Screenshots showed messages sent around 9:50 a.m. Wednesday from an account under Dayeh University's domain, displaying the name "Liu Fang-chun"; the private university in Changhua County said an initial investigation found an alumnus' account had sent a large number of emails and appeared hacked, and it suspended the account. Taiwan's representative office in Italy said Taiwanese agencies were willing to provide technical assistance to Italian investigators. This is the earliest public reporting naming the Taiwanese sender account that Hudson Rock later tied to infostealer data.

findings.title: Hoax bomb threats made to schools in Scotland, Northern Ireland and Italy
findings.summary_md: The Guardian reported that schools in Scotland, Northern Ireland, the Republic of Ireland, and Italy received hoax bomb threats, with the Italian email containing the words "we have come to annihilate you" and signed by "Mikhail Andropov, leader of the Vilayat of Misoginistan." The PSNI considered the risk to the public low, while the Garda Siochana assessed the threat as "not credible" and did not call for evacuations. Italy's national association of headteachers called the threat "clearly fake" but warned of the disruption caused by such messages.
